newsitem.title: USA: Child injured in airbag incident.
newsitem.headline: Child injured in airbag incident.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they were investigating an accident in which a child suffered a severe neck injury when a driver's side airbag deployed.

Capt. Michael Books of the Elkhart County Sheriff's office in Indiana said 4-year-old Kyle Davis suffered the injury when a car driven by his mother, Christine, was involved in a three-car crash on Tuesday.
The child was strapped in the middle of the front seat of the Ford Taurus, a legal position under Indiana law, which requires car seats only for children through the age of three.

Most of the publicity involving airbag injuries has concerned devices on the passenger side, a problem that has led to recommendations that children not sit in the front passenger side of airbag-equipped cars.
The child suffered a cracked vertebra and was taken by helicopter to a hospital for treatment.

Air bags have been credited with saving 1,900 lives since 1986, but they have also been blamed for the deaths of 40 children and 27 adults since 1990, primarily because of the rapid speed and extreme force with which they deploy in even minor accidents.
